```markdown
# xNglo Unicode 9 Scripts Mapping

## Overview

This file documents the mapping between **Unicode code points** of 9 Indian
writing scripts and their **xNglo phonetic representations**. The mapping is
used by `hsciistr_file.ts` in the `uL2xin38()` method for script conversion.

## Unicode Script Blocks

| # | Script | Block Start | Block End | Unicode Range |
|---|--------|-------------|-----------|---------------|
| 1 | Hindi (Devanagari) | 0x0900 | 0x097F | U+0900-U+097F |
| 2 | Bengali | 0x0980 | 0x09FF | U+0980-U+09FF |
| 3 | Gurmukhi (Punjabi) | 0x0A00 | 0x0A7F | U+0A00-U+0A7F |
| 4 | Gujarati | 0x0A80 | 0x0AFF | U+0A80-U+0AFF |
| 5 | Oriya | 0x0B00 | 0x0B7F | U+0B00-U+0B7F |
| 6 | Tamil | 0x0B80 | 0x0BFF | U+0B80-U+0BFF |
| 7 | Telugu | 0x0C00 | 0x0C7F | U+0C00-U+0C7F |
| 8 | Kannada | 0x0C80 | 0x0CFF | U+0C80-U+0CFF |
| 9 | Malayalam | 0x0D00 | 0x0D7F | U+0D00-U+0D7F |

## Block Structure

Each script block is **128 code points** (0x00-0x7F). The offset within the
block determines the character type:

| Offset Range | Type |
|--------------|------|
| 0x00-0x04 | Reserved / Special |
| 0x05-0x14 | Vowels (16) |
| 0x15-0x39 | Consonants (37) |
| 0x3A-0x3D | Special signs |
| 0x3E-0x4C | Vowel signs / Matras (15) |
| 0x4D | Virama (Halant) |
| 0x4E-0x5F | Additional / Nukta variants |
| 0x60-0x63 | Additional vowels |
| 0x64-0x65 | Punctuation |
| 0x66-0x6F | Digits (0-9) |
| 0x70-0x7F | Script-specific |

## xNglo Mapping Table

### Vowels (Offsets 0x05-0x14)

| Offset | Unicode | xNglo | Type |
|--------|---------|-------|------|
| 0x05 | अ | x | standalone vowel (schwa) |
| 0x06 | आ | a | vowel |
| 0x07 | इ | _i | vowel |
| 0x08 | ई | _i | vowel (long) |
| 0x09 | उ | _u | vowel |
| 0x0A | ऊ | _u | vowel (long) |
| 0x0B | ऋ | ri | vocalic r |
| 0x0C | ऌ | li | vocalic l |
| 0x0F | ए | _e | vowel |
| 0x10 | ऐ | _e | vowel |
| 0x13 | ओ | o | vowel |
| 0x14 | औ | ou | vowel |

### Consonants (Offsets 0x15-0x39)

| Offset | Unicode | xNglo | Type |
|--------|---------|-------|------|
| 0x15 | क | k | unaspirated |
| 0x16 | ख | K | aspirated |
| 0x17 | ग | g | unaspirated |
| 0x18 | घ | gh | aspirated |
| 0x19 | ङ | N | nasal |
| 0x1A | च | c | unaspirated |
| 0x1B | छ | C | aspirated |
| 0x1C | ज | z | unaspirated |
| 0x1D | झ | Z | aspirated |
| 0x1E | ञ | n | nasal |
| 0x1F | ट | t | retroflex |
| 0x20 | ठ | T | aspirated retroflex |
| 0x21 | ड | d | retroflex |
| 0x22 | ढ | D | aspirated retroflex |
| 0x23 | ण | n | retroflex nasal |
| 0x24 | त | j | dental |
| 0x25 | थ | J | aspirated dental |
| 0x26 | द | q | dental |
| 0x27 | ध | Q | aspirated dental |
| 0x28 | न | n | dental nasal |
| 0x2A | प | p | unaspirated |
| 0x2B | फ | f | aspirated |
| 0x2C | ब | b | unaspirated |
| 0x2D | भ | B | aspirated |
| 0x2E | म | m | nasal |
| 0x2F | य | y | semi-vowel |
| 0x30 | र | r | liquid |
| 0x32 | ल | l | liquid |
| 0x33 | ळ | l | retroflex liquid |
| 0x35 | व | w | semi-vowel |
| 0x36 | श | S | sibilant |
| 0x37 | ष | s | retroflex sibilant |
| 0x38 | स | s | dental sibilant |
| 0x39 | ह | v | glottal |

### Matras / Vowel Signs (Offsets 0x3E-0x4C)

| Offset | Unicode | xNglo | Meaning |
|--------|---------|-------|---------|
| 0x3E | ा | a | aa matra |
| 0x3F | ि | i | i matra |
| 0x40 | ी | i | ii matra |
| 0x41 | ु | u | u matra |
| 0x42 | ू | u | uu matra |
| 0x43 | ृ | ri | vocalic r matra |
| 0x47 | े | e | e matra |
| 0x48 | ै | ye | ai matra |
| 0x49 | ॉ | o | o matra |
| 0x4B | ो | o | oo matra |
| 0x4C | ौ | ou | au matra |
| 0x4D | ् | (empty) | virama / halant |

### Digits (Offsets 0x66-0x6F)

| Offset | Unicode | xNglo |
|--------|---------|-------|
| 0x66 | ० | 0 |
| 0x67 | १ | 1 |
| 0x68 | २ | 2 |
| 0x69 | ३ | 3 |
| 0x6A | ४ | 4 |
| 0x6B | ५ | 5 |
| 0x6C | ६ | 6 |
| 0x6D | ७ | 7 |
| 0x6E | ८ | 8 |
| 0x6F | ९ | 9 |

## Conversion Logic (uL2xin38)

```
Input: Unicode text (any of 9 Indian scripts)
↓
For each character:

1. Get Unicode code point
2. Determine block: li = (codepoint / 0x80) >> 0
3. Determine offset: ki = codepoint % 0x80
4. If li in range (0x12-0x1A): lookup in 9-scripts table
5. If li == 0x1B: lookup in 10th script (Sinhala) table
6. Else: keep character as-is
   ↓
   Post-processing (unicode\_india\_10scripts\_to\_xnglo\_india\_post)
   ↓
   Output: xNglo text
```

## Key Features

1. **Unified mapping** - All 9 scripts map to same xNglo representation
2. **Offset-based** - Same offset = same phonetic value across scripts
3. **Simple lookup** - Array indexing by offset (0x00-0x7F)
4. **Post-processing** - Handles special cases (schwa deletion, nasal rules)

## Usage

```typescript
const converter = new hsciistr();
converter.set_input("नमस्ते");
await converter.duztr();
console.log(converter.output['xi38']);  // xNglo output
```

## Conversion Logic (uL2xin38)

Input: Unicode text (any of 9 Indian scripts)
↓
For each character:

Get Unicode code point

Determine block: li = (codepoint / 0x80) >> 0

Determine offset: ki = codepoint % 0x80

If li in range (0x12-0x1A): lookup in 9-scripts table

If li == 0x1B: lookup in 10th script (Sinhala) table

Else: keep character as-is
↓
Post-processing (unicode_india_10scripts_to_xnglo_india_post)
↓
Output: xNglo text


## Key Features

1. **Unified mapping** – All 9 scripts map to same xNglo representation
2. **Offset-based** – Same offset = same phonetic value across scripts
3. **Simple lookup** – Array indexing by offset (0x00-0x7F)
4. **Post-processing** – Handles special cases (schwa deletion, nasal rules)

## Usage

```typescript
const converter = new hsciistr();
converter.set_input("नमस्ते");
await converter.duztr();
console.log(converter.output['xi38']);  // xNglo output
```

| 0x35 | व | w | semi-vowel |
| 0x36 | श | S | sibilant |
| 0x37 | ष | s | retroflex sibilant |
| 0x38 | स | s | dental sibilant |
| 0x39 | ह | v | glottal |

### Matras / Vowel Signs (Offsets 0x3E–0x4C)

| Offset | Unicode | xNglo | Meaning |
|--------|---------|-------|---------|
| 0x3E | ा | a | aa matra |
| 0x3F | ि | i | i matra |
| 0x40 | ी | i | ii matra |
| 0x41 | ु | u | u matra |
| 0x42 | ू | u | uu matra |
| 0x43 | ृ | ri | vocalic r matra |
| 0x47 | े | e | e matra |
| 0x48 | ै | ye | ai matra |
| 0x49 | ॉ | o | o matra |
| 0x4B | ो | o | oo matra |
| 0x4C | ौ | ou | au matra |
| 0x4D | ् | (empty) | virama / halant |

### Digits (Offsets 0x66–0x6F)

| Offset | Unicode | xNglo |
|--------|---------|-------|
| 0x66 | ० | 0 |
| 0x67 | १ | 1 |
| 0x68 | २ | 2 |
| 0x69 | ३ | 3 |
| 0x6A | ४ | 4 |
| 0x6B | ५ | 5 |
| 0x6C | ६ | 6 |
| 0x6D | ७ | 7 |
| 0x6E | ८ | 8 |
| 0x6F | ९ | 9 |

## Conversion Logic (uL2xin38)

Input: Unicode text (any of 9 Indian scripts)
↓
For each character:

Get Unicode code point

Determine block: li = (codepoint / 0x80) >> 0

Determine offset: ki = codepoint % 0x80

If li in range (0x12-0x1A): lookup in 9-scripts table

If li == 0x1B: lookup in 10th script (Sinhala) table

Else: keep character as-is
↓
Post-processing (unicode_india_10scripts_to_xnglo_india_post)
↓
Output: xNglo text


## Key Features

1. **Unified mapping** – All 9 scripts map to same xNglo representation
2. **Offset-based** – Same offset = same phonetic value across scripts
3. **Simple lookup** – Array indexing by offset (0x00-0x7F)
4. **Post-processing** – Handles special cases (schwa deletion, nasal rules)

## Usage

```typescript
const converter = new hsciistr();
converter.set_input("नमस्ते");
await converter.duztr();
console.log(converter.output['xi38']);  // xNglo output
```

## References
TypeScript source: <https://github.com/zawa8/htrlib/blob/main/src/hsciistr_file.ts>

CSV data: <https://github.com/zawa8/xnglo/blob/main/dxta/xNglo_phoneme_grapheme.csv>

Unicode charts: <https://unicode.org/charts/>

#### DeepSeek:
# C++ OOP (Object-Oriented Programming) in Hindi

## 1. Class (क्लास)

Class ek **blueprint** hai - jaise ek template jisse objects bante hain.

```cpp
class Car {
    // Member variables (attributes)
    string brand;
    int year;
    
    // Member function (method)
    void start() {
        cout << "Car started!" << endl;
    }
};
```

**Hindi me:** Class ek sancha (सांचा) hai. Jaise ek "Car" ka design - usme brand, year hota hai aur start karne ki ability hoti hai.

---

## 2. Object (ऑब्जेक्ट)

Object class ka **instance** hai - real cheez jo memory me banti hai.

```cpp
int main() {
    Car myCar;        // Object bana
    myCar.brand = "Toyota";
    myCar.start();    // Method call
}
```

**Hindi me:** Class blueprint hai, object us blueprint se bani asli car hai.

---

## 3. Encapsulation (एनकैप्सुलेशन)

Data aur methods ko ek saath class me band karna, aur data ko **private** rakhna.

```cpp
class BankAccount {
private:
    double balance;    // Private - bahar se access nahi
    
public:
    void deposit(double amount) {
        balance += amount;
    }
    
    double getBalance() {
        return balance;
    }
};
```

**Hindi me:** Data ko chhupa kar rakhna (data hiding) aur sirf safe methods se access dena.

---

## 4. Inheritance (इनहेरिटेंस)

Ek class dusri class ke **properties inherit** karti hai.

```cpp
// Parent class
class Vehicle {
public:
    string brand;
    void honk() {
        cout << "Beep beep!" << endl;
    }
};

// Child class
class Car : public Vehicle {
public:
    int doors;
};
```

**Hindi me:** Jaise bachcha maa-baap ke gun (properties) leta hai. Car, Vehicle ke saare features le leti hai.

---

## 5. Polymorphism (पॉलीमॉर्फिज्म)

Ek hi naam ke **multiple forms** - same function alag-alag kaam karta hai.

### Function Overloading:
```cpp
int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
double add(double a, double b) { return a + b; }
```

### Method Overriding:
```cpp
class Animal {
public:
    virtual void speak() {
        cout << "Animal speaks" << endl;
    }
};

class Dog : public Animal {
public:
    void speak() override {
        cout << "Woof!" << endl;
    }
};
```

**Hindi me:** Ek hi kaam alag-alag tarike se karna. Dog bhi speak karta hai, lekin alag awaz me.

---

## 6. Abstraction (एब्सट्रैक्शन)

Sirf **zaroori details** dikhana, complex cheezein chhupana.

```cpp
class CoffeeMachine {
public:
    void makeCoffee() {
        boilWater();
        brewBeans();
        pour();
    }
    
private:
    void boilWater() { /* complex logic */ }
    void brewBeans() { /* complex logic */ }
    void pour() { /* complex logic */ }
};
```

User sirf `makeCoffee()` call karta hai - use nahi pata ki andar kya hota hai.

**Hindi me:** Complex cheezein chhupa kar simple interface dena.

---

## 7. Constructor (कंस्ट्रक्टर)

Object banate hi **automatically call** hota hai.

```cpp
class Car {
public:
    string brand;
    
    // Constructor
    Car(string b) {
        brand = b;
        cout << "Car created: " << brand << endl;
    }
    
    // Destructor
    ~Car() {
        cout << "Car destroyed: " << brand << endl;
    }
};
```

**Hindi me:** Jaise ghar banate hi lights on ho jayein - constructor object creation par chalta hai.

---

## 8. Complete Example


```cpp
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Student {
private:
    string name;
    int rollNo;
    
public:
    // Constructor
    Student(string n, int r) {
        name = n;
        rollNo = r;
    }
    
    // Getter
    string getName() {
        return name;
    }
    
    // Display
    void display() {
        cout << "Name: " << name << endl;
        cout << "Roll No: " << rollNo << endl;
    }
};

int main() {
    Student s1("Ramesh", 101);
    Student s2("Suresh", 102);
    
    s1.display();
    s2.display();
    
    return 0;
}
```

---

## Summary Table

| OOP Concept   | Hindi Meaning | Simple Example                    |
| ------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Class         | सांचा         | Car ka design                     |
| Object        | वस्तु         | Asli car                          |
| Encapsulation | डेटा छिपाना   | Bank account ka balance           |
| Inheritance   | विरासत        | Car, Vehicle se features leti hai |
| Polymorphism  | बहुरूपता      | Dog alag awaz me speak karta hai  |
| Abstraction   | सारांश        | Coffee machine ka button          |
| Constructor   | निर्माता      | Object banate hi chalta hai       |

---

Kya aapko kisi specific concept me aur detail chahiye?


#### You:
https://github.com/zawa8/vskii_rust4/tree/cpp4 Suru krje h. isme gcc ke kisi smaller old wersion se start krna h. kyese kre . ya fir gcc fork krke nya repo bnae.

#### DeepSeek:
Aapka sawal bahut important hai - **GCC fork karke cpp4 compiler** banane ke liye sahi approach kya ho.

## Approach 1: GCC Fork (Recommended)

### Step 1: GCC ka chhota version clone karein

GCC ke **purane chhote versions** se start karna better hai kyunki:

- Code base chhota hota hai
- Build time kam
- Samajhna aasan

**Recommended versions:**

- GCC 4.8 (2013) - simple, well-documented
- GCC 5.4 (2016) - stable, smaller
- GCC 7.5 (2019) - moderate

### Step 2: GitHub par fork karein


```bash
# GCC mirror clone karein (shallow clone)
git clone --depth 1 --branch releases/gcc-5.4.0 https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc.git cpp4-gcc

cd cpp4-gcc
```

### Step 3: Naya repo banayein

GitHub par **`cpp4-gcc`** naam se naya repo banayein, phir:

```bash
# Remote change karein
git remote remove origin
git remote add origin https://github.com/zawa8/cpp4-gcc.git

# Push karein
git push -u origin main
```

---

## Approach 2: Sirf GCC ka Frontend Copy karein (Better)

GCC ka pura code (\~100 MB+) copy karne ki zaroorat nahi. Sirf **C++ frontend** copy karein:

```bash
# Sirf cp/ directory (C++ frontend) copy karein
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc.git gcc-temp
cd gcc-temp

# cp directory ko naye repo me copy karein
cp -r gcc/cp/ /path/to/cpp4-compiler/
```

---

## Approach 3: Submodule use karein


```bash
# vskii_rust4 repo me GCC ko submodule banayein
cd vskii_rust4
git submodule add https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc.git gcc
git submodule update --init --depth 1
```

---

## Abhi ke liye Best Plan:

### 1. Naya repo banayein: `cpp4-gcc`

### 2. GCC 5.4 ka shallow clone karein:


```bash
git clone --depth 1 --branch releases/gcc-5.4.0 https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc.git cpp4-gcc
cd cpp4-gcc
rm -rf .git
git init
git remote add origin https://github.com/zawa8/cpp4-gcc.git
```

### 3. C++ frontend ko modify karein:

Main changes:

- `gcc/cp/lex.cc` - Lexical analysis (hskii characters)
- `gcc/cp/parser.cc` - Grammar rules (cplong instead of float)
- `gcc/cp/typeck.cc` - Type checking

### 4. Build karein:


```bash
mkdir build && cd build

#### DeepSeek:
# GCC Frontend Structure - cpp4 Compiler Ke Liye

## GCC Frontend Kya Hai?

GCC compiler 3 parts me divided hai:

1. **Frontend** - Language-specific (C++, C, Java, etc.)
2. **Middle-end** - Language-independent optimization
3. **Backend** - Machine code generation

Aapko sirf **Frontend** change karna hai - jisme C++ ka code cpp4 me convert hoga.

---

## GCC Directory Structure


```
gcc/
├── gcc/
│   ├── cp/          ← C++ Frontend (YAHAN KAAM KARNA HAI)
│   │   ├── lex.cc       → Lexical analysis (tokenization)
│   │   ├── parser.cc    → Grammar rules
│   │   ├── typeck.cc    → Type checking
│   │   ├── decl.cc      → Declarations
│   │   ├── cp-tree.h    → Header definitions
│   │   └── Make-lang.in → Build config
│   ├── c/           → C Frontend
│   ├── common/      → Shared code
│   └── ...
```

---

## Key Files To Change

### 1. `gcc/cp/lex.cc` - Lexical Analysis

**Kaam:** Source code ko tokens me todna

**Changes needed:**

- hskii hex digits (L,Y,V,W,P,F) ko recognize karna
- `cplong` keyword add karna
- Programming symbols (E,U,I,O,M,X,A,H) ko operators me convert karna

**Example change:**
```cpp
// Purana: float keyword
if (token == "float") return FLOAT;

// Naya: cplong keyword
if (token == "cplong") return CPLONG;
```

---

### 2. `gcc/cp/parser.cc` - Grammar Rules

**Kaam:** Tokens se syntax tree banana

**Changes needed:**

- `float` ki jagah `cplong` accept karna
- cplong literals parse karna (jaise `5V,FF,10.04.40`)

**Example change:**
```cpp
// Purana: float declaration
case FLOAT:
    type = float_type;
    break;

// Naya: cplong declaration
case CPLONG:
    type = cplong_type;
    break;
```

---

### 3. `gcc/cp/typeck.cc` - Type Checking

**Kaam:** Ensure types sahi hain

**Changes needed:**

- cplong ke liye arithmetic operations define karna
- No overflow checking (cplong me overflow nahi hota)

---

### 4. `gcc/cp/cp-tree.h` - Header Definitions

**Kaam:** New types aur constants define karna

**Changes needed:**
```cpp
// Naya type add karein
#define CPLONG_TYPE  /* cplong ka type */
```

---

## Lexical Changes Detail (Most Important)

### hskii Hex Digits Recognition


```cpp
// In lex.cc - digit recognition me change

// Purana: sirf 0-9 aur A-F
if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') return DIGIT;
if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F') return HEX_DIGIT;

// Naya: hskii digits bhi add karein
if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') return DIGIT;
if (c == 'L') return HEX_DIGIT;  // 10
if (c == 'Y') return HEX_DIGIT;  // 11
if (c == 'V') return HEX_DIGIT;  // 12
if (c == 'W') return HEX_DIGIT;  // 13
if (c == 'P') return HEX_DIGIT;  // 14
if (c == 'F') return HEX_DIGIT;  // 15
```

---

### Programming Symbols Mapping


```cpp
// In lex.cc - operator recognition

// E → ==
// U → !=
// I → >=
// O → <=
// M → &&
// X → ||
// A → =>
// H → ++

if (c == 'E' && next == '=') return EQ_OP;
if (c == 'U' && next == '!') return NE_OP;
// ... etc
```

---

## Build Process


```bash
# 1. GCC source download
git clone --depth 1 --branch releases/gcc-5.4.0 https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc.git cpp4-gcc

# 2. cpp4 frontend directory create
cd cpp4-gcc/gcc
mkdir cp4
cp -r cp/* cp4/

# 3. Configure with new language
cd ..
mkdir build && cd build
../configure --enable-languages=cpp4

# 4. Build
make -j4
```

---

## Minimal Working Example

### cpp4 Source Code:
```cpp
main()
{
    cplong.meksimum_layers = 16;
    cplong a = 5V,5V,FF,10.04.40;
}
```

### Lexical Analysis:
```
main → IDENTIFIER
( → LPAREN
) → RPAREN
{ → LBRACE
cplong → CPLONG (naya keyword)
. → DOT
meksimum_layers → IDENTIFIER
= → ASSIGN
16 → NUMBER
; → SEMICOLON
cplong → CPLONG
a → IDENTIFIER
= → ASSIGN
5V → CPLONG_LITERAL
, → COMMA
5V → CPLONG_LITERAL
...
```

```markdown
# cpp4-gcc

cpp4 compiler - GCC fork for hskii encoding.

## About

cpp4 is a C++ variant that uses:
- **cplong** instead of float (arbitrary-precision numbers)
- **hskii hex digits** (L,Y,V,W,P,F)
- **hskii programming symbols** (E,U,I,O,M,X,A,H)

## Key Features

- Float-less (no float/double)
- Overflow-less (unlimited precision via cplong)
- hskii phonetic encoding support

## Status

Development in progress. Based on GCC 5.4.0.

## References

- hskii encoding: https://github.com/zawa8/vskii_rust4
- Keyboard: https://github.com/zawa8/xNglobord
- Number system: https://github.com/zawa8/plong
```

## `lex.cc` me kya changes karne hain:

### Change 1: hskii Hex Digits recognize karna

GCC ke `lex.cc` me ye function dhundhein jo **hex digits** (0-9, A-F) ko recognize karta hai.

Purane code me aisa kuch hoga:

if ((c >= '0' && c <= '9') ||

    c == 'W' || c == 'P' || c == 'F')
```

#### DeepSeek:
Good morning! Aapne ek important problem batayi hai - **cplong number representation** me confusion hai. Main analyze karta hoon.

## Problem Analysis:

### aapke cpp4 code me alag-alag formats hain:


```
-5V,FF,FF:6      ← colon (:) use hua hai
5:5V.FF.PF       ← colon aur period mixed
5V,0.0.6         ← comma aur period mixed
```

### Ye inconsistent hai. Humein ek **standard format** decide karna hoga.

---

## Proposed Standard Format for cplong:

### Option A: Comma for integer, Period for fractional (purana wala)


```
-5V,FF,FF.6
5.5V.FF.PF
5V,0.0.6
```

### Option B: Colon for layer separator (naya)


```
-5V,FF,FF:6     ← : ke baad fractional part
5:5V.FF.PF
5V,0:0.6
```

### Option C: Simple and consistent


```
-5V.FF.FF.6     ← sirf period use karo
5.5V.FF.PF
5V.0.0.6
```

---

## Mera Recommendation:

**Option C** - sirf period (`.`) use karo. Ye sabse simple hai:

```
cplong a = -5V.FF.FF.6;
cplong b = 5.5V.FF.PF;
cplong c = 5V.0.0.6;
```

## cplong Standard Format:

### Default (start\_pl = 0):
```
cplong a = -5V.FF.FF.6;
```

### Explicit start\_pl (using colon):
```
cplong a = -5V.FF.FF.6:-7;
```

---

## Rules:

1. **`.`** = digit separator
2. **`:`** = start\_pl (starting precision layer)
3. **`-`** = negative sign (number ke pehle)
4. **Default start\_pl** = 0 (agar colon nahi hai)
5. **`:-7`** = start\_pl -7 (colon ke baad ka number)

---

## Examples:

| Code            | Meaning                 |
| --------------- | ----------------------- |
| `5V.FF.FF.6`    | start\_pl = 0 (default) |
| `5V.FF.FF.6:-7` | start\_pl = -7          |
| `-5V.FF.FF.6:2` | negative, start\_pl = 2 |

## cplong Format with Explicit start\_pl:


```
cplong a = -5V.FF.FF.6:-7;
```

### Meaning:

- `-` = negative
- `5V` = pehla digit
- `.` = digit separator
- `:-7` = pehla digit ka power **-7**

### So:
```
5V × 10^(-7)  (jahan 10 = hexadecimal 16)
FF × 10^(-8)
FF × 10^(-9)
6  × 10^(-10)
```

### Yaani:
```
-5V.FF.FF.6:-7 = -(5V × 16⁻⁷ + FF × 16⁻⁸ + FF × 16⁻⁹ + 6 × 16⁻¹⁰)
```

---

## Default case:


```
cplong a = -5V.FF.FF.6;   // start_pl = 0 (default)
```

Ye barabar hai:
```
5V × 16⁰ + FF × 16⁻¹ + FF × 16⁻² + 6 × 16⁻³
```

| Format  | Meaning                   |
| ------- | ------------------------- |
| `:-7`   | Pehla digit 16⁻⁷ se shuru |
| `:2`    | Pehla digit 16² se shuru  |
| Default | Pehla digit 16⁰ se shuru  |

## `src/cplong.rs` (Updated)


```rust
//! cplong: hskii arbitrary-precision number.
//!
//! Format: "-5V.FF.FF.6:-7"
//! - Period '.' separates digits
//! - Colon ':' followed by start_prisizxn_leyr (power of 16)
//! - Default start_prisizxn_leyr = 0
//! - Each digit is 0-255 (displayed as hex pair)

use crate::digit::Digit;
use crate::error::CplongError;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cplong {
    pub wlyu: Vec<u8>,
    pub start_prisizxn_leyr: i8,
    pub is_negetiw: bool,
}

impl Cplong {
    pub const MAX_SIZE: usize = 1024;

    /// Parse cplong from string like "-5V.FF.FF.6:-7"
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, CplongError> {
        let s = s.trim();
        if s.is_empty() {
            return Err(CplongError::EmptyInput);
        }

        // Parse sign
        let (is_negetiw, rest) = if let Some(stripped) = s.strip_prefix('-') {
            (true, stripped)
        } else {
            (false, s)
        };

        // Split number and explicit start_pl
        let (num_part, explicit_pl) = if let Some(idx) = rest.find(':') {
            let (n, p) = rest.split_at(idx);
            let p = p.trim_start_matches(':');
            let pl = p.parse::<i8>().map_err(|_| CplongError::InvalidFormat(s.to_string()))?;
            (n, Some(pl))
        } else {
            (rest, None)
        };

        // Split digits by period
        let digits: Vec<&str> = num_part.split('.').collect();
        if digits.is_empty() {
            return Err(CplongError::EmptyInput);
        }

        // Parse each digit
        let mut wlyu = Vec::new();
        for d in digits {
            let byte = parse_hex_pair(d)?;
            wlyu.push(byte);
        }

        // start_prisizxn_leyr: explicit or default 0
        let start_prisizxn_leyr = explicit_pl.unwrap_or(0);

        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu,
            start_prisizxn_leyr,
            is_negetiw,
        })
    }

    /// Display in hskii format
    pub fn to_hskii_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut result = String::new();
        if self.is_negetiw {
            result.push('-');
        }

        for (i, &byte) in self.wlyu.iter().enumerate() {
            if i > 0 {
                result.push('.');
            }
            let high = byte >> 4;
            let low = byte & 0x0F;
            result.push(digit_to_char(high));
            result.push(digit_to_char(low));
        }

        // Add explicit start_pl if not 0
        if self.start_prisizxn_leyr != 0 {
            result.push(':');
            result.push_str(&self.start_prisizxn_leyr.to_string());
        }

        result
    }

    /// Convert to decimal string (for debugging)
    pub fn to_decimal_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut result = 0.0f64;
        let mut power = self.start_prisizxn_leyr as f64;

        for &byte in &self.wlyu {
            result += (byte as f64) * (16.0f64).powf(power);
            power -= 1.0;
        }

        if self.is_negetiw {
            result = -result;
        }

        format!("{}", result)
    }
}

fn parse_hex_pair(s: &str) -> Result<u8, CplongError> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.trim().chars().collect();
    
    match chars.len() {
        1 => {
            let d = Digit::from_char(chars[0]).ok_or(CplongError::InvalidCharacter(chars[0]))?;
            Ok(d.value())
        }
        2 => {
            let high = Digit::from_char(chars[0]).ok_or(CplongError::InvalidCharacter(chars[0]))?;
            let low = Digit::from_char(chars[1]).ok_or(CplongError::InvalidCharacter(chars[1]))?;
            Ok((high.value() << 4) | low.value())
        }
        _ => Err(CplongError::InvalidFormat(s.to_string()))
    }
}

fn digit_to_char(d: u8) -> char {
    Digit::new(d).unwrap().to_char()
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Cplong {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}", self.to_hskii_string())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_default_pl() {
        let a = Cplong::parse("5V.FF").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF]);
        assert_eq!(a.start_prisizxn_leyr, 0);
        assert!(!a.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_explicit_pl() {
        let a = Cplong::parse("-5V.FF.FF.6:-7").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x06]);
        assert_eq!(a.start_prisizxn_leyr, -7);
        assert!(a.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_positive_pl() {
        let a = Cplong::parse("5V.FF:2").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF]);
        assert_eq!(a.start_prisizxn_leyr, 2);
        assert!(!a.is_negetiw);
    }
}
```

// src/cplong.rs
//
// Implements parsing and formatting for the "cplong" type using the HSkii digit mapping.
//
// Format examples:
//  "5V.FF"           -> wlyu = [0x5C, 0xFF], start_pl = 0
//  "-5V.FF.FF.6:-7"  -> wlyu = [0x5C, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x06], start_pl = -7
//  "5V.FF:2"         -> wlyu = [0x5C, 0xFF], start_pl = 2
//
// Rules implemented:
//  - Period '.' separates digit tokens.
//  - Optional colon ':' followed by start_prisizxn_leyr (power of 16). Default start_pl = 0.
//  - Tokens are 1 or 2 HSkii hex digits mapping to values 0..=255 (byte).
//    Single-digit tokens represent values 0..=15 (e.g. "6" -> 0x06).
//  - Accepts optional leading '+' or '-' before the first digit; it is ignored for wlyu parsing.
//  - HSkii digit mapping:
//      '0'..'9' -> 0..9
//      'L' -> 10
//      'Y' -> 11
//      'V' -> 12
//      'W' -> 13
//      'P' -> 14
//      'F' -> 15
//    (case-insensitive)

use std::fmt;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cplong {
    pub wlyu: Vec<u8>,
    pub start_pl: i32,
}

impl Cplong {
    /// Parse a string into a Cplong.
    ///
    /// Returns Err(String) with an explanatory message on parse failure.
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
        if s.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err("empty input".into());
        }

        // Split off start_pl if present (use the last colon as separator)
        let mut parts = s.rsplitn(2, ':');
        let maybe_start = parts.next(); // rightmost piece
        let maybe_main = parts.next(); // remaining left side, if any

        let (main_str, start_str_opt) = match (maybe_main, maybe_start) {
            (Some(left), Some(right)) => (left, Some(right)),
            (None, Some(right)) => (right, None), // no colon present
            _ => return Err("invalid input parsing".into()),
        };

        // If there was a colon, start_str_opt is Some(start_text)
        let start_pl = if let Some(start_text) = start_str_opt {
            // If there was a colon, start_text is the rightmost piece
            // Accept signed integer
            let st = start_text.trim();
            if st.is_empty() {
                return Err("empty start_pl after ':'".into());
            }
            st.parse::<i32>()
                .map_err(|e| format!("invalid start_pl '{}': {}", st, e))?
        } else {
            0
        };

        // main_str may have an optional leading sign; ignore it for the bytes
        let main = main_str.trim();
        if main.is_empty() {
            return Err("no digits found".into());
        }
        let mut chars = main.chars();
        let first_char = chars.next().unwrap();
        let (main_without_sign, _had_sign) = if first_char == '+' || first_char == '-' {
            (chars.as_str(), true)
        } else {
            (main, false)
        };

        let mut wlyu: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();

        for token in main_without_sign.split('.') {
            let tok = token.trim();
            if tok.is_empty() {
                return Err("empty token between dots".into());
            }
            let val = Cplong::parse_token(tok)?;
            wlyu.push(val);
        }

        Ok(Cplong { wlyu, start_pl })
    }

    /// Convert a token (1 or 2 HSkii digits) to a byte value.
    fn parse_token(tok: &str) -> Result<u8, String> {
        let tok = tok.trim();
        if tok.is_empty() {
            return Err("empty token".into());
        }
        let mut chars = tok.chars().collect::<Vec<char>>();
        if chars.len() > 2 {
            return Err(format!("token too long '{}'", tok));
        }
        // Map characters to nibble values
        let map_nibble = |c: char| -> Result<u8, String> {
            let cu = c.to_ascii_uppercase();
            match cu {
                '0'..='9' => Ok((cu as u8) - b'0'),
                'L' => Ok(10),
                'Y' => Ok(11),
                'V' => Ok(12),
                'W' => Ok(13),
                'P' => Ok(14),
                'F' => Ok(15),
                _ => Err(format!("invalid HSkii digit '{}'", c)),
            }
        };

        if chars.len() == 1 {
            let n = map_nibble(chars[0])?;
            Ok(n) // single nibble => value 0..15
        } else {
            let hi = map_nibble(chars[0])?;
            let lo = map_nibble(chars[1])?;
            let val = hi
                .checked_mul(16)
                .and_then(|x| x.checked_add(lo))
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("byte overflow for token '{}'", tok))?;
            Ok(val)
        }
    }

    /// Format as HSkii string using the HSkii digit map.
    /// For bytes < 16, a single HSkii digit is emitted (e.g. 6 -> "6").
    /// For bytes >= 16, two HSkii digits are emitted (e.g. 0x5C -> "5V").
    /// The tokens are joined by '.'. If start_pl != 0 it is appended after a colon.
    pub fn to_hskii_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for (i, &b) in self.wlyu.iter().enumerate() {
            if i != 0 {
                out.push('.');
            }
            if b < 16 {
                out.push(nibble_to_hskii((b & 0xF) as u8));
            } else {
                let hi = (b >> 4) & 0xF;
                let lo = b & 0xF;
                out.push(nibble_to_hskii(hi as u8));
                out.push(nibble_to_hskii(lo as u8));
            }
        }
        if self.start_pl != 0 {
            out.push(':');
            out.push_str(&self.start_pl.to_string());
        }
        out
    }

    /// A simple decimal debug string: decimal bytes separated by '.' with optional ":<start_pl>"
    /// Example: [92,255] start_pl=0 => "92.255"
    pub fn to_decimal_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for (i, &b) in self.wlyu.iter().enumerate() {
            if i != 0 {
                out.push('.');
            }
            out.push_str(&b.to_string());
        }
        if self.start_pl != 0 {
            out.push(':');
            out.push_str(&self.start_pl.to_string());
        }
        out
    }
}

fn nibble_to_hskii(n: u8) -> char {
    match n {
        0..=9 => (b'0' + n) as char,
        10 => 'L',
        11 => 'Y',
        12 => 'V',
        13 => 'W',
        14 => 'P',
        15 => 'F',
        _ => '?',
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Cplong {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(&self.to_hskii_string())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::Cplong;

    #[test]
    fn parse_simple_two_tokens() {
        let s = "5V.FF";
        let c = Cplong::parse(s).expect("parse failed");
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF]);
        assert_eq!(c.start_pl, 0);
        assert_eq!(c.to_hskii_string(), "5V.FF");
        assert_eq!(c.to_decimal_string(), "92.255");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_with_colon_negative_start() {
        let s = "-5V.FF.FF.6:-7";
        let c = Cplong::parse(s).expect("parse failed");
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x06]);
        assert_eq!(c.start_pl, -7);
        // Note: leading '-' is not included in to_hskii_string output; colon start_pl is preserved
        assert_eq!(c.to_hskii_string(), "5V.FF.FF.6:-7");
        assert_eq!(c.to_decimal_string(), "92.255.255.6:-7");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_with_colon_positive_start() {
        let s = "5V.FF:2";
        let c = Cplong::parse(s).expect("parse failed");
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF]);
        assert_eq!(c.start_pl, 2);
        assert_eq!(c.to_hskii_string(), "5V.FF:2");
        assert_eq!(c.to_decimal_string(), "92.255:2");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parse_single_digit_token() {
        let s = "A.6"; // 'A' is not a valid HSkii digit -> should fail
        assert!(Cplong::parse(s).is_err());

        let s2 = "6.5";
        let r = Cplong::parse(s2).expect("parse failed");
        assert_eq!(r.wlyu, vec![6, 5]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn hskii_roundtrip() {
        let s = "L.Y.V.W.P.F.0.9.5V.6";
        // L=10,Y=11,V=12,W=13,P=14,F=15 so tokens: 10,11,12,13,14,15,0,9,0x5C,6
        let c = Cplong::parse(s).expect("parse failed");
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu[0..6], [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15]);
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu[6], 0);
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu[7], 9);
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu[8], 0x5C);
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu[9], 6);
        // Roundtrip formatting should produce the same HSkii for these token styles
        assert_eq!(c.to_hskii_string(), "L.Y.V.W.P.F.0.9.5V.6");
    }
}

//! cplong: hskii arbitrary-precision number.
//!
//! Format: "-2P,5V,67,5V.67.78.89"
//! - Comma separates integer digits (base-256 bytes)
//! - Period separates fractional digits
//! - Each digit is displayed as hex pair (2P, 5V, 67, etc.)

use crate::digit::Digit;
use crate::error::CplongError;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cplong {
    /// Array of base-256 digits (each 0-255)
    pub wlyu: Vec<u8>,
    /// Starting precision layer (power of 256 for first digit)
    pub start_prisizxn_leyr: i8,
    /// Negative flag
    pub is_negetiw: bool,
}

impl Cplong {
    pub const MAX_SIZE: usize = 1024;

    /// Create new Cplong from string like "-2P,5V,67,5V.67.78.89"
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, CplongError> {
        let s = s.trim();
        if s.is_empty() {
            return Err(CplongError::EmptyInput);
        }

        // Parse sign
        let (is_negetiw, rest) = if let Some(stripped) = s.strip_prefix('-') {
            (true, stripped)
        } else {
            (false, s)
        };

        // Split integer and fractional parts
        let (int_part, frac_part) = match rest.split_once('.') {
            Some((i, f)) => (i, Some(f)),
            None => (rest, None),
        };

        // Parse integer digits
        let int_digits: Vec<u8> = if int_part.is_empty() {
            vec![]
        } else {
            int_part
                .split(',')
                .map(parse_hex_pair)
                .collect::<Result<Vec<u8>, CplongError>>()?
        };

        // Parse fractional digits
        let frac_digits: Vec<u8> = if let Some(f) = frac_part {
            if f.is_empty() {
                vec![]
            } else {
                f.split('.')
                    .map(parse_hex_pair)
                    .collect::<Result<Vec<u8>, CplongError>>()?
            }
        } else {
            vec![]
        };

        // start_prisizxn_leyr = (number of integer digits - 1)
        let start_prisizxn_leyr = int_digits.len() as i8 - 1;

        // Combine digits
        let mut wlyu = int_digits;
        wlyu.extend(frac_digits);

        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu,
            start_prisizxn_leyr,
            is_negetiw,
        })
    }

    /// Convert to decimal string (for debugging)
    pub fn to_decimal_string(&self) -> String {
        // Simplified - converts base-256 to decimal for small numbers
        let mut result = 0.0f64;
        let mut power = self.start_prisizxn_leyr as f64;

        for &byte in &self.wlyu {
            result += (byte as f64) * (256.0f64).powf(power);
            power -= 1.0;
        }

        if self.is_negetiw {
            result = -result;
        }

        format!("{}", result)
    }

    /// Addition
    pub fn add(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, CplongError> {
        let a = self.to_decimal_string().parse::<f64>().map_err(|_| CplongError::Overflow)?;
        let b = other.to_decimal_string().parse::<f64>().map_err(|_| CplongError::Overflow)?;
        Cplong::from_f64(a + b)
    }

    /// Subtraction
    pub fn sub(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, CplongError> {
        let a = self.to_decimal_string().parse::<f64>().map_err(|_| CplongError::Overflow)?;
        let b = other.to_decimal_string().parse::<f64>().map_err(|_| CplongError::Overflow)?;
        Cplong::from_f64(a - b)
    }

    /// Multiplication
    pub fn mul(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, CplongError> {
        let a = self.to_decimal_string().parse::<f64>().map_err(|_| CplongError::Overflow)?;
        let b = other.to_decimal_string().parse::<f64>().map_err(|_| CplongError::Overflow)?;
        Cplong::from_f64(a * b)
    }

    /// Division
    pub fn div(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, CplongError> {
        let a = self.to_decimal_string().parse::<f64>().map_err(|_| CplongError::Overflow)?;
        let b = other.to_decimal_string().parse::<f64>().map_err(|_| CplongError::Overflow)?;
        if b == 0.0 {
            return Err(CplongError::DivisionByZero);
        }
        Cplong::from_f64(a / b)
    }

    /// Convert from f64 to Cplong (simplified)
    pub fn from_f64(value: f64) -> Result<Cplong, CplongError> {
        let is_negetiw = value < 0.0;
        let abs_val = value.abs();

        // Convert to hex string
        let int_part = abs_val.trunc() as u64;
        let frac_part = abs_val.fract();

        let int_hex = format!("{:X}", int_part);
        let mut wlyu = Vec::new();

        // Parse hex pairs
        let padded = if int_hex.len() % 2 == 0 {
            int_hex.clone()
        } else {
            format!("0{}", int_hex)
        };

        for i in (0..padded.len()).step_by(2) {
            let pair = &padded[i..i + 2];
            let byte = u8::from_str_radix(pair, 16).map_err(|_| CplongError::InvalidFormat(pair.to_string()))?;
            wlyu.push(byte);
        }

        if frac_part > 0.0 {
            let frac_hex = format!("{:X}", (frac_part * 256.0 * 256.0 * 256.0 * 256.0) as u64);
            // Simplified - add fractional bytes
            let padded_frac = if frac_hex.len() % 2 == 0 {
                frac_hex.clone()
            } else {
                format!("0{}", frac_hex)
            };
            for i in (0..padded_frac.len()).step_by(2) {
                let pair = &padded_frac[i..i + 2];
                if let Ok(byte) = u8::from_str_radix(pair, 16) {
                    wlyu.push(byte);
                }
            }
        }

        let start_prisizxn_leyr = (wlyu.len() as i8 / 2) - 1;

        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu,
            start_prisizxn_leyr,
            is_negetiw,
        })
    }

    /// Display in hskii format
    pub fn to_hskii_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut result = String::new();
        if self.is_negetiw {
            result.push('-');
        }

        let int_count = (self.start_prisizxn_leyr + 1).max(0) as usize;

        for (i, &byte) in self.wlyu.iter().enumerate() {
            if i == int_count && int_count > 0 {
                result.push('.');
            } else if i > 0 && i < int_count {
                result.push(',');
            }

            let high = byte >> 4;
            let low = byte & 0x0F;
            result.push(digit_to_char(high));
            result.push(digit_to_char(low));
        }

        result
    }
}

/// Parse hex pair like "2P" -> 46
fn parse_hex_pair(s: &str) -> Result<u8, CplongError> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.trim().chars().collect();
    
    match chars.len() {
        1 => {
            // Single digit: 0-15
            let d = Digit::from_char(chars[0]).ok_or(CplongError::InvalidCharacter(chars[0]))?;
            Ok(d.value())
        }
        2 => {
            // Hex pair: 0-255
            let high = Digit::from_char(chars[0]).ok_or(CplongError::InvalidCharacter(chars[0]))?;
            let low = Digit::from_char(chars[1]).ok_or(CplongError::InvalidCharacter(chars[1]))?;
            Ok((high.value() << 4) | low.value())
        }
        _ => Err(CplongError::InvalidFormat(s.to_string()))
    }
}

fn digit_to_char(d: u8) -> char {
    Digit::new(d).unwrap().to_char()
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Cplong {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}", self.to_hskii_string())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_simple() {
        let a = Cplong::parse("5V").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.wlyu, vec![0x5C]);
        assert_eq!(a.start_prisizxn_leyr, 0);
        assert!(!a.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_negative() {
        let b = Cplong::parse("-6").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(b.wlyu, vec![6]);
        assert_eq!(b.start_prisizxn_leyr, 0);
        assert!(b.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_complex() {
        let c = Cplong::parse("-2P,5V.67").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu, vec![0x2E, 0x5C, 0x67]);
        assert_eq!(c.start_prisizxn_leyr, 1);
        assert!(c.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_subtraction() {
        let a = Cplong::parse("6").unwrap();
        let b = Cplong::parse("5V").unwrap();
        let d = a.sub(&b).unwrap();
        assert!(d.is_negetiw);
    }

pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
    let s = s.trim();
    if s.is_empty() {
        return Err("empty input".into());
    }

    // Split off optional start_prisizxn_leyr after the last colon, if present.
    let (main_part, start_part_opt) = match s.rfind(':') {
        Some(idx) => {
            let (left, right) = s.split_at(idx);
            // right starts with ':'
            (left, Some(&right[1..]))
        }
        None => (s, None),
    };

    // Parse start_prisizxn_leyr if provided, default 0.
    let start_prisizxn_leyr: i32 = if let Some(st) = start_part_opt {
        let st = st.trim();
        if st.is_empty() {
            return Err("empty start_prisizxn_leyr after ':'".into());
        }
        st.parse::<i32>()
            .map_err(|e| format!("invalid start_prisizxn_leyr '{}': {}", st, e))?
    } else {
        0
    };

    // Handle optional leading sign on main_part
    let main_trim = main_part.trim();
    let (mut is_negetiw, digits_str) = if main_trim.starts_with('-') {
        (true, main_trim[1..].trim())
    } else if main_trim.starts_with('+') {
        (false, main_trim[1..].trim())
    } else {
        (false, main_trim)
    };

    // If there are no digits, return an error (require at least one digit token)
    if digits_str.is_empty() {
        return Err("no digit tokens found".into());
    }

    let mut wlyu: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    for token in digits_str.split('.') {
        let tok = token.trim();
        if tok.is_empty() {
            return Err("empty digit token (consecutive or trailing '.')".into());
        }
        let b = Cplong::parse_token(tok)?;
        wlyu.push(b);
    }

    Ok(Cplong {
        wlyu,
        start_prisizxn_leyr,
        is_negetiw,
    })
}

pub fn to_hskii_string(&self) -> String {
    let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(self.wlyu.len());
    for &b in &self.wlyu {
        if b < 16 {
            // single nibble -> single HSkii digit
            let c = nibble_to_hskii((b & 0x0F) as u8);
            parts.push(c.to_string());
        } else {
            let hi = (b >> 4) & 0x0F;
            let lo = b & 0x0F;
            let mut s = String::with_capacity(2);
            s.push(nibble_to_hskii(hi as u8));
            s.push(nibble_to_hskii(lo as u8));
            parts.push(s);
        }
    }

    let mut out = parts.join(".");

    if self.start_prisizxn_leyr != 0 {
        out.push(':');
        out.push_str(&self.start_prisizxn_leyr.to_string());
    }

    if self.is_negetiw {
        out.insert(0, '-');
    }

    out
}

//! cplong: hskii arbitrary-precision number.
//!
//! Format: "-5V.FF.FF.6:-7"
//! - Period '.' separates all digits
//! - Colon ':' followed by start_prisizxn_leyr (power of 16)
//! - Default start_prisizxn_leyr = 0
//! - Each digit is 0-255 (hex pair using hskii digits)

use std::fmt;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cplong {
    pub wlyu: Vec<u8>,
    pub start_prisizxn_leyr: i32,
    pub is_negetiw: bool,
}

impl Cplong {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
        let s = s.trim();
        if s.is_empty() {
            return Err("empty input".into());
        }

        let (main_part, start_part_opt) = match s.rfind(':') {
            Some(idx) => {
                let (left, right) = s.split_at(idx);
                (left, Some(&right[1..]))
            }
            None => (s, None),
        };

        let start_prisizxn_leyr: i32 = if let Some(st) = start_part_opt {
            let st = st.trim();
            if st.is_empty() {
                return Err("empty start_prisizxn_leyr after ':'".into());
            }
            st.parse::<i32>()
                .map_err(|e| format!("invalid start_prisizxn_leyr '{}': {}", st, e))?
        } else {
            0
        };

        let main_trim = main_part.trim();
        let (is_negetiw, digits_str) = if main_trim.starts_with('-') {
            (true, main_trim[1..].trim())
        } else if main_trim.starts_with('+') {
            (false, main_trim[1..].trim())
        } else {
            (false, main_trim)
        };

        if digits_str.is_empty() {
            return Err("no digit tokens found".into());
        }

        let mut wlyu: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        for token in digits_str.split('.') {
            let tok = token.trim();
            if tok.is_empty() {
                return Err("empty digit token".into());
            }
            let b = parse_token(tok)?;
            wlyu.push(b);
        }

        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu,
            start_prisizxn_leyr,
            is_negetiw,
        })
    }

    pub fn to_hskii_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(self.wlyu.len());
        for &b in &self.wlyu {
            if b < 16 {
                let c = nibble_to_hskii((b & 0x0F) as u8);
                parts.push(c.to_string());
            } else {
                let hi = (b >> 4) & 0x0F;
                let lo = b & 0x0F;
                let mut s = String::with_capacity(2);
                s.push(nibble_to_hskii(hi as u8));
                s.push(nibble_to_hskii(lo as u8));
                parts.push(s);
            }
        }

        let mut out = parts.join(".");

        if self.start_prisizxn_leyr != 0 {
            out.push(':');
            out.push_str(&self.start_prisizxn_leyr.to_string());
        }

        if self.is_negetiw {
            out.insert(0, '-');
        }

        out
    }

    pub fn to_decimal_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for (i, &b) in self.wlyu.iter().enumerate() {
            if i != 0 {
                out.push('.');
            }
            out.push_str(&b.to_string());
        }
        if self.start_prisizxn_leyr != 0 {
            out.push(':');
            out.push_str(&self.start_prisizxn_leyr.to_string());
        }
        if self.is_negetiw {
            out.insert(0, '-');
        }
        out
    }
}

fn parse_token(tok: &str) -> Result<u8, String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = tok.trim().chars().collect();
    match chars.len() {
        1 => {
            let d = map_nibble(chars[0])?;
            Ok(d)
        }
        2 => {
            let hi = map_nibble(chars[0])?;
            let lo = map_nibble(chars[1])?;
            Ok((hi << 4) | lo)
        }
        _ => Err(format!("invalid token '{}'", tok)),
    }
}

fn map_nibble(c: char) -> Result<u8, String> {
    match c.to_ascii_uppercase() {
        '0'..='9' => Ok((c as u8) - b'0'),
        'L' => Ok(10),
        'Y' => Ok(11),
        'V' => Ok(12),
        'W' => Ok(13),
        'P' => Ok(14),
        'F' => Ok(15),
        _ => Err(format!("invalid hskii digit '{}'", c)),
    }
}

fn nibble_to_hskii(n: u8) -> char {
    match n {
        0..=9 => (b'0' + n) as char,
        10 => 'L',
        11 => 'Y',
        12 => 'V',
        13 => 'W',
        14 => 'P',
        15 => 'F',
        _ => '?',
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Cplong {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}", self.to_hskii_string())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_default_pl() {
        let a = Cplong::parse("5V.FF").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF]);
        assert_eq!(a.start_prisizxn_leyr, 0);
        assert!(!a.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_negative_with_pl() {
        let b = Cplong::parse("-5V.FF.FF.6:-7").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(b.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x06]);
        assert_eq!(b.start_prisizxn_leyr, -7);
        assert!(b.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_positive_pl() {
        let c = Cplong::parse("5V.FF:2").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF]);
        assert_eq!(c.start_prisizxn_leyr, 2);
        assert!(!c.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_roundtrip() {
        let s = "-5V.FF.FF.6:-7";
        let c = Cplong::parse(s).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.to_hskii_string(), s);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_single_digit() {
        let c = Cplong::parse("6.5").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu, vec![6, 5]);
        assert_eq!(c.to_hskii_string(), "6.5");
    }
}

        let main_trim = main_part.trim();
        let (is_negetiw, digits_str) = if main_trim.starts_with('-') {
            (true, main_trim[1..].trim())
        } else if main_trim.starts_with('+') {
            (false, main_trim[1..].trim())
        } else {
            (false, main_trim)
        };

        if digits_str.is_empty() {
            return Err("no digit tokens found".into());
        }

        let mut wlyu: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        for token in digits_str.split('.') {
            let tok = token.trim();
            if tok.is_empty() {
                return Err("empty digit token".into());
            }
            let b = parse_token(tok)?;
            wlyu.push(b);
        }

        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu,
            start_prisizxn_leyr,
            is_negetiw,
        })
    }

    pub fn to_hskii_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(self.wlyu.len());
        for &b in &self.wlyu {
            if b < 16 {
                let c = nibble_to_hskii((b & 0x0F) as u8);
                parts.push(c.to_string());
            } else {
                let hi = (b >> 4) & 0x0F;
                let lo = b & 0x0F;
                let mut s = String::with_capacity(2);
                s.push(nibble_to_hskii(hi as u8));
                s.push(nibble_to_hskii(lo as u8));
                parts.push(s);
            }
        }

        let mut out = parts.join(".");

        if self.start_prisizxn_leyr != 0 {
            out.push(':');
            out.push_str(&self.start_prisizxn_leyr.to_string());
        }

        if self.is_negetiw {
            out.insert(0, '-');
        }

        out
    }

    pub fn to_decimal_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for (i, &b) in self.wlyu.iter().enumerate() {
            if i != 0 {
                out.push('.');
            }
            out.push_str(&b.to_string());
        }
        if self.start_prisizxn_leyr != 0 {
            out.push(':');
            out.push_str(&self.start_prisizxn_leyr.to_string());
        }
        if self.is_negetiw {
            out.insert(0, '-');
        }
        out
    }
}

fn parse_token(tok: &str) -> Result<u8, String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = tok.trim().chars().collect();
    match chars.len() {
        1 => {
            let d = map_nibble(chars[0])?;
            Ok(d)
        }
        2 => {
            let hi = map_nibble(chars[0])?;
            let lo = map_nibble(chars[1])?;
            Ok((hi << 4) | lo)
        }
        _ => Err(format!("invalid token '{}'", tok)),
    }
}

fn map_nibble(c: char) -> Result<u8, String> {
    match c.to_ascii_uppercase() {
        '0'..='9' => Ok((c as u8) - b'0'),
        'L' => Ok(10),
        'Y' => Ok(11),
        'V' => Ok(12),
        'W' => Ok(13),
        'P' => Ok(14),
        'F' => Ok(15),
        _ => Err(format!("invalid hskii digit '{}'", c)),
    }
}

fn nibble_to_hskii(n: u8) -> char {
    match n {
        0..=9 => (b'0' + n) as char,
        10 => 'L',
        11 => 'Y',
        12 => 'V',
        13 => 'W',
        14 => 'P',
        15 => 'F',
        _ => '?',
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Cplong {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}", self.to_hskii_string())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_default_pl() {
        let a = Cplong::parse("5V.FF").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF]);
        assert_eq!(a.start_prisizxn_leyr, 0);
        assert!(!a.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_negative_with_pl() {
        let b = Cplong::parse("-5V.FF.FF.6:-7").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(b.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x06]);
        assert_eq!(b.start_prisizxn_leyr, -7);
        assert!(b.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_positive_pl() {
        let c = Cplong::parse("5V.FF:2").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu, vec![0x5C, 0xFF]);
        assert_eq!(c.start_prisizxn_leyr, 2);
        assert!(!c.is_negetiw);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_roundtrip() {
        let s = "-5V.FF.FF.6:-7";
        let c = Cplong::parse(s).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.to_hskii_string(), s);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_single_digit() {
        let c = Cplong::parse("6.5").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(c.wlyu, vec![6, 5]);
        assert_eq!(c.to_hskii_string(), "6.5");
    }
}

// Add these methods to impl Cplong block:

/// Addition of two cplong numbers (exact)
pub fn add(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
    if self.is_negetiw == other.is_negetiw {
        // Same sign: add absolute values
        let mut result = Cplong::add_abs(self, other)?;
        result.is_negetiw = self.is_negetiw;
        Ok(result)
    } else {
        // Different signs: subtract absolute values
        if Cplong::abs_compare(self, other) >= 0 {
            let mut result = Cplong::sub_abs(self, other)?;
            result.is_negetiw = self.is_negetiw;
            Ok(result)
        } else {
            let mut result = Cplong::sub_abs(other, self)?;
            result.is_negetiw = other.is_negetiw;
            Ok(result)
        }
    }
}

/// Subtraction of two cplong numbers
pub fn sub(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
    let mut neg_other = other.clone();
    neg_other.is_negetiw = !neg_other.is_negetiw;
    self.add(&neg_other)
}

/// Multiplication of two cplong numbers (exact)
pub fn mul(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
    let result_is_neg = self.is_negetiw != other.is_negetiw;
    
    // Multiply each digit (school method)
    let mut result_digits = vec![0u8; self.wlyu.len() + other.wlyu.len()];
    
    for i in 0..self.wlyu.len() {
        for j in 0..other.wlyu.len() {
            let product = (self.wlyu[i] as u32) * (other.wlyu[j] as u32);
            let pos = i + j;
            let mut carry = product;
            let mut k = pos;
            
            while carry > 0 {
                let sum = result_digits[k] as u32 + carry;
                result_digits[k] = (sum & 0xFF) as u8;
                carry = sum >> 8;
                k += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Remove trailing zeros
    while result_digits.len() > 1 && result_digits.last() == Some(&0) {
        result_digits.pop();
    }
    result_digits.reverse();
    
    // Calculate new start_pl
    let new_start = self.start_prisizxn_leyr + other.start_prisizxn_leyr + 1;
    
    Ok(Cplong {
        wlyu: result_digits,
        start_prisizxn_leyr: new_start,
        is_negetiw: result_is_neg,
    })
}

/// Division of two cplong numbers (exact up to max_layers)
pub fn div(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
    // Check division by zero
    if other.wlyu.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
        return Err("division by zero".into());
    }
    
    let result_is_neg = self.is_negetiw != other.is_negetiw;
    let max_layers = 32; // Default precision
    
    // Convert to base-16 digits for division
    let dividend = Cplong::abs_to_base16(self);
    let divisor = Cplong::abs_to_base16(other);
    
    // Long division algorithm
    let mut quotient = Vec::new();
    let mut remainder = Vec::new();
    
    for digit in &dividend {
        remainder.push(*digit);
        
        let mut q = 0u8;
        while Cplong::compare_base16(&remainder, &divisor) >= 0 {
            remainder = Cplong::subtract_base16(&remainder, &divisor);
            q += 1;
        }
        quotient.push(q);
    }
    
    // Handle fractional part
    let mut frac_digits = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..max_layers {
        remainder.push(0);
        let mut q = 0u8;
        while Cplong::compare_base16(&remainder, &divisor) >= 0 {
            remainder = Cplong::subtract_base16(&remainder, &divisor);
            q += 1;
        }
        frac_digits.push(q);
    }
    
    // Combine integer and fractional parts
    let mut result_digits = quotient;
    result_digits.extend(frac_digits);
    
    Ok(Cplong {
        wlyu: result_digits,
        start_prisizxn_leyr: 0,
        is_negetiw: result_is_neg,
    })
}

// Helper methods
fn add_abs(a: &Cplong, b: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
    let mut result = vec![0u8; a.wlyu.len().max(b.wlyu.len()) + 1];
    let mut carry = 0u16;
    
    let max_len = a.wlyu.len().max(b.wlyu.len());
    for i in 0..max_len {
        let da = if i < a.wlyu.len() { a.wlyu[i] as u16 } else { 0 };
        let db = if i < b.wlyu.len() { b.wlyu[i] as u16 } else { 0 };
        let sum = da + db + carry;
        result[i] = (sum & 0xFF) as u8;
        carry = sum >> 8;
    }
    
    if carry > 0 {
        result[max_len] = carry as u8;
    } else {
        result.pop();
    }
    
    Ok(Cplong {
        wlyu: result,
        start_prisizxn_leyr: a.start_prisizxn_leyr,
        is_negetiw: false,
    })
}

fn sub_abs(a: &Cplong, b: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
    // Assumes a >= b
    let mut result = vec![0u8; a.wlyu.len()];
    let mut borrow = 0i16;
    
    for i in 0..a.wlyu.len() {
        let da = a.wlyu[i] as i16;
        let db = if i < b.wlyu.len() { b.wlyu[i] as i16 } else { 0 };
        let diff = da - db - borrow;
        if diff < 0 {
            borrow = 1;
            result[i] = (diff + 256) as u8;
        } else {
            borrow = 0;
            result[i] = diff as u8;
        }
    }
    
    while result.len() > 1 && result.last() == Some(&0) {
        result.pop();
    }
    
    Ok(Cplong {
        wlyu: result,
        start_prisizxn_leyr: a.start_prisizxn_leyr,
        is_negetiw: false,
    })
}

fn abs_compare(a: &Cplong, b: &Cplong) -> i32 {
    if a.wlyu.len() != b.wlyu.len() {
        return a.wlyu.len() as i32 - b.wlyu.len() as i32;
    }
    for i in (0..a.wlyu.len()).rev() {
        if a.wlyu[i] != b.wlyu[i] {
            return a.wlyu[i] as i32 - b.wlyu[i] as i32;
        }
    }
    0
}

fn abs_to_base16(c: &Cplong) -> Vec<u8> {
    // Convert each byte to two base-16 nibbles
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for &b in &c.wlyu {
        result.push((b >> 4) & 0x0F);
        result.push(b & 0x0F);
    }
    result
}

fn compare_base16(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> i32 {
    if a.len() != b.len() {
        return a.len() as i32 - b.len() as i32;
    }
    for i in 0..a.len() {
        if a[i] != b[i] {
            return a[i] as i32 - b[i] as i32;
        }
    }
    0
}

fn subtract_base16(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut result = a.to_vec();
    let mut borrow = 0i16;
    
    for i in (0..a.len()).rev() {
        let da = a[i] as i16;
        let db = if i < b.len() { b[i] as i16 } else { 0 };
        let diff = da - db - borrow;
        if diff < 0 {
            borrow = 1;
            result[i] = (diff + 16) as u8;
        } else {
            borrow = 0;
            result[i] = diff as u8;
        }
    }
    
    while result.len() > 1 && result[0] == 0 {
        result.remove(0);
    }
    result
}

```rust
//! cplong: hskii arbitrary-precision number.
//!
//! Format: "-5V.FF.FF.6:-7"
//! - Period '.' separates all digits
//! - Colon ':' followed by start_prisizxn_leyr (power of 16)
//! - Default start_prisizxn_leyr = 0
//! - Each digit is 0-255 (hex pair using hskii digits)

use std::fmt;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cplong {
    pub wlyu: Vec<u8>,
    pub start_prisizxn_leyr: i32,
    pub is_negetiw: bool,
}

impl Cplong {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
        let s = s.trim();
        if s.is_empty() {
            return Err("empty input".into());
        }

        let (main_part, start_part_opt) = match s.rfind(':') {
            Some(idx) => {
                let (left, right) = s.split_at(idx);
                (left, Some(&right[1..]))
            }
            None => (s, None),
        };

        let start_prisizxn_leyr: i32 = if let Some(st) = start_part_opt {
            let st = st.trim();
            if st.is_empty() {
                return Err("empty start_prisizxn_leyr after ':'".into());
            }
            st.parse::<i32>()
                .map_err(|e| format!("invalid start_prisizxn_leyr '{}': {}", st, e))?
        } else {
            0
        };

        let main_trim = main_part.trim();
        let (is_negetiw, digits_str) = if main_trim.starts_with('-') {
            (true, main_trim[1..].trim())
        } else if main_trim.starts_with('+') {
            (false, main_trim[1..].trim())
        } else {
            (false, main_trim)
        };

        if digits_str.is_empty() {
            return Err("no digit tokens found".into());
        }

        let mut wlyu: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        for token in digits_str.split('.') {
            let tok = token.trim();
            if tok.is_empty() {
                return Err("empty digit token".into());
            }
            let b = parse_token(tok)?;
            wlyu.push(b);
        }

        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu,
            start_prisizxn_leyr,
            is_negetiw,
        })
    }

    pub fn to_hskii_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(self.wlyu.len());
        for &b in &self.wlyu {
            if b < 16 {
                let c = nibble_to_hskii((b & 0x0F) as u8);
                parts.push(c.to_string());
            } else {
                let hi = (b >> 4) & 0x0F;
                let lo = b & 0x0F;
                let mut s = String::with_capacity(2);
                s.push(nibble_to_hskii(hi as u8));
                s.push(nibble_to_hskii(lo as u8));
                parts.push(s);
            }
        }

        let mut out = parts.join(".");

        if self.start_prisizxn_leyr != 0 {
            out.push(':');
            out.push_str(&self.start_prisizxn_leyr.to_string());
        }

        if self.is_negetiw {
            out.insert(0, '-');
        }

        out
    }

    pub fn to_decimal_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        for (i, &b) in self.wlyu.iter().enumerate() {
            if i != 0 {
                out.push('.');
            }
            out.push_str(&b.to_string());
        }
        if self.start_prisizxn_leyr != 0 {
            out.push(':');
            out.push_str(&self.start_prisizxn_leyr.to_string());
        }
        if self.is_negetiw {
            out.insert(0, '-');
        }
        out
    }

    pub fn add(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
        if self.is_negetiw == other.is_negetiw {
            let mut result = Self::add_abs(self, other)?;
            result.is_negetiw = self.is_negetiw;
            Ok(result)
        } else {
            if Self::abs_compare(self, other) >= 0 {
                let mut result = Self::sub_abs(self, other)?;
                result.is_negetiw = self.is_negetiw;
                Ok(result)
            } else {
                let mut result = Self::sub_abs(other, self)?;
                result.is_negetiw = other.is_negetiw;
                Ok(result)
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn sub(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
        let mut neg_other = other.clone();
        neg_other.is_negetiw = !neg_other.is_negetiw;
        self.add(&neg_other)
    }

    pub fn mul(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
        let result_is_neg = self.is_negetiw != other.is_negetiw;
        let mut result_digits = vec![0u32; self.wlyu.len() + other.wlyu.len()];
        
        for i in 0..self.wlyu.len() {
            for j in 0..other.wlyu.len() {
                let product = (self.wlyu[i] as u32) * (other.wlyu[j] as u32);
                let pos = i + j;
                let mut carry = product;
                let mut k = pos;
                
                while carry > 0 {
                    let sum = result_digits[k] + carry;
                    result_digits[k] = sum & 0xFF;
                    carry = sum >> 8;
                    k += 1;
                }
            }
        }
        
        while result_digits.len() > 1 && result_digits.last() == Some(&0) {
            result_digits.pop();
        }
        
        let mut wlyu: Vec<u8> = result_digits.iter().map(|&x| x as u8).collect();
        wlyu.reverse();
        
        let new_start = self.start_prisizxn_leyr + other.start_prisizxn_leyr + 1;
        
        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu,
            start_prisizxn_leyr: new_start,
            is_negetiw: result_is_neg,
        })
    }

    pub fn div(&self, other: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
        if other.wlyu.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
            return Err("division by zero".into());
        }
        
        let result_is_neg = self.is_negetiw != other.is_negetiw;
        let max_layers = 16;
        
        let dividend = Self::abs_to_base16(self);
        let divisor = Self::abs_to_base16(other);
        
        let mut quotient = Vec::new();
        let mut remainder = Vec::new();
        
        for digit in &dividend {
            remainder.push(*digit);
            let mut q = 0u8;
            while Self::compare_base16(&remainder, &divisor) >= 0 {
                remainder = Self::subtract_base16(&remainder, &divisor);
                q += 1;
            }
            quotient.push(q);
        }
        
        let mut frac_digits = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..max_layers {
            remainder.push(0);
            let mut q = 0u8;
            while Self::compare_base16(&remainder, &divisor) >= 0 {
                remainder = Self::subtract_base16(&remainder, &divisor);
                q += 1;
            }
            frac_digits.push(q);
        }
        
        let mut result_digits = quotient;
        result_digits.extend(frac_digits);
        
        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu: result_digits,
            start_prisizxn_leyr: 0,
            is_negetiw: result_is_neg,
        })
    }

    fn add_abs(a: &Cplong, b: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
        let mut result = vec![0u8; a.wlyu.len().max(b.wlyu.len()) + 1];
        let mut carry = 0u16;
        let max_len = a.wlyu.len().max(b.wlyu.len());
        
        for i in 0..max_len {
            let da = if i < a.wlyu.len() { a.wlyu[i] as u16 } else { 0 };
            let db = if i < b.wlyu.len() { b.wlyu[i] as u16 } else { 0 };
            let sum = da + db + carry;
            result[i] = (sum & 0xFF) as u8;
            carry = sum >> 8;
        }
        
        if carry > 0 {
            result[max_len] = carry as u8;
        } else {
            result.pop();
        }
        
        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu: result,
            start_prisizxn_leyr: a.start_prisizxn_leyr,
            is_negetiw: false,
        })
    }

    fn sub_abs(a: &Cplong, b: &Cplong) -> Result<Cplong, String> {
        let mut result = vec![0u8; a.wlyu.len()];
        let mut borrow = 0i16;
        
        for i in 0..a.wlyu.len() {
            let da = a.wlyu[i] as i16;
            let db = if i < b.wlyu.len() { b.wlyu[i] as i16 } else { 0 };
            let diff = da - db - borrow;
            if diff < 0 {
                borrow = 1;
                result[i] = (diff + 256) as u8;
            } else {
                borrow = 0;
                result[i] = diff as u8;
            }
        }
        
        while result.len() > 1 && result.last() == Some(&0) {
            result.pop();
        }
        
        Ok(Cplong {
            wlyu: result,
            start_prisizxn_leyr: a.start_prisizxn_leyr,
            is_negetiw: false,
        })
    }

    fn abs_compare(a: &Cplong, b: &Cplong) -> i32 {
        if a.wlyu.len() != b.wlyu.len() {
            return a.wlyu.len() as i32 - b.wlyu.len() as i32;
        }
        for i in (0..a.wlyu.len()).rev() {
            if a.wlyu[i] != b.wlyu[i] {
                return a.wlyu[i] as i32 - b.wlyu[i] as i32;
            }
        }
        0
    }

    fn abs_to_base16(c: &Cplong) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        for &b in &c.wlyu {
            result.push((b >> 4) & 0x0F);
            result.push(b & 0x0F);
        }
        result
    }

    fn compare_base16(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> i32 {
        if a.len() != b.len() {
            return a.len() as i32 - b.len() as i32;
        }
        for i in 0..a.len() {
            if a[i] != b[i] {
                return a[i] as i32 - b[i] as i32;
            }
        }
        0
    }

    fn subtract_base16(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut result = a.to_vec();
        let mut borrow = 0i16;
        
        for i in (0..a.len()).rev() {
            let da = a[i] as i16;
            let db = if i < b.len() { b[i] as i16 } else { 0 };
            let diff = da - db - borrow;
            if diff < 0 {
                borrow = 1;
                result[i] = (diff + 16) as u8;
            } else {
                borrow = 0;
                result[i] = diff as u8;
            }
        }
        
        while result.len() > 1 && result[0] == 0 {
            result.remove(0);
        }
        result
    }
}

fn parse_token(tok: &str) -> Result<u8, String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = tok.trim().chars().collect();
    match chars.len() {
        1 => {
            let d = map_nibble(chars[0])?;
            Ok(d)
        }
        2 => {
            let hi = map_nibble(chars[0])?;
            let lo = map_nibble(chars[1])?;
            Ok((hi << 4) | lo)
        }
        _ => Err(format!("invalid token '{}'", tok)),
    }
}

fn map_nibble(c: char) -> Result<u8, String> {
    match c.to_ascii_uppercase() {
        '0'..='9' => Ok((c as u8) - b'0'),
        'L' => Ok(10),
        'Y' => Ok(11),
        'V' => Ok(12),
        'W' => Ok(13),
        'P' => Ok(14),
        'F' => Ok(15),
        _ => Err(format!("invalid hskii digit '{}'", c)),
    }
}

fn nibble_to_hskii(n: u8) -> char {
    match n {
        0..=9 => (b'0' + n) as char,
        10 => 'L',
        11 => 'Y',
        12 => 'V',
        13 => 'W',
        14 => 'P',
        15 => 'F',
        _ => '?',
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Cplong {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}", self.to_hskii_string())
    }
}
